# Liquid assets waiting period

The liquid assets waiting period is between one and 13 weeks.

It applies if you have funds equal to or more than either:

- $5,500 if you’re single with no dependants
- $11,000 if have a partner or you’re single with dependants.

Liquid assets are any funds readily available to you or your partner. This includes money your employer owes you.

The liquid assets waiting period may apply if you’re making a new claim for one of the following payments:

- [JobSeeker Payment](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/jobseeker-payment)
- [Youth Allowance](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/youth-allowance)
- [Austudy](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/austudy).

We determine your liquid assets waiting period based on your personal situation and the amount of funds you have. The table below shows the number of weeks you need to wait based on your liquid assets.

| Number of weeks you’ll need to wait under the Liquid Assets Waiting Period | If you have a partner or you’re single – with dependants and your liquid assets are | If you’re single with no dependants and your liquid assets are |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NIL | $0 to $10,999 | $0 to $5,499 |
| 1 | $11,000 to $11,999 | $5,500 to $5,999 |
| 2 | $12,000 to $12,999 | $6,000 to $6,499 |
| 3 | $13,000 to $13,999 | $6,500 to $6,999 |
| 4 | $14,000 to $14,999 | $7,000 to $7,499 |
| 5 | $15,000 to $15,999 | $7,500 to $7,999 |
| 6 | $16,000 to $16,999 | $8,000 to $8,499 |
| 7 | $17,000 to $17,999 | $8,500 to $8,999 |
| 8 | $18,000 to $18,999 | $9,000 to $9,499 |
| 9 | $19,000 to $19,999 | $9,500 to $9,999 |
| 10 | $20,000 to $20,999 | $10,000 to $10,499 |
| 11 | $21,000 to $21,999 | $10,500 to $10,999 |
| 12 | $22,000 to $22,999 | $11,000 to $11,499 |
| 13 | $23,000 or more | $11,500 or more |

We’ll tell you how long you have to wait when your claim is assessed.

## Exemptions or waivers

We may waive the liquid assets waiting period if you’re experiencing [severe financial hardship](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/severe-financial-hardship-provisions?context=51411) because of unavoidable or reasonable expenses.

You may be exempt if any of these apply:

- you or your partner have been subject to a liquid assets waiting period that started within the last 12 months
- you transfer from one payment to another within a 14 day period
- you have self-served this waiting period before claiming
- you qualified for [JobSeeker Payment](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/jobseeker-payment) after getting another payment.

### If your partner has recently died

This waiting period may not apply if you’re recently widowed and you submitted your claim within 14 weeks of your partner’s death.

If you were pregnant at the time of your partner’s death, you must have submitted the claim within either:

- 14 weeks of the death of your partner
- before the pregnancy ends, whichever is the longest period.
